# BRIEF

## User-Facing Goal

Help restaurant owners understand the product in one visual scan: choose a menu format, see what HostingQr sets up, follow the shared benefits, and understand how future changes work.

## Success Criteria

- The opening question is immediately visible below the fixed navigation.
- The two product paths and their differences are visually distinct and easy to compare.
- Shared Translations, QR Code, and Google Maps steps clearly merge into one path.
- The final Easy Changes step branches back into format-specific instructions.
- The flow remains readable and touch-friendly on narrow mobile screens.
- Both example actions open the intended live examples.
- Both menu choices show an immediate phone-sized visual example without requiring a click.
- The shared steps visually demonstrate translations, a usable QR code, and a Google business menu link instead of relying on icons alone.

## UX Notes

Use compact rounded nodes, simple inline icons, and visible connector lines rather than a conventional card grid. Keep paired nodes side-by-side on mobile to preserve the branching story, while limiting copy and using responsive type and spacing.

Use static previews instead of live iframes so homepage visits do not increment example-project analytics or load two complete public pages on mobile.

Keep shared-step visuals compact and stack them below the explanatory copy on narrow screens. The QR should be genuinely scannable and link to the live Web Page Menu example.

Refined direction: keep each shared-step visual on the left at all viewport sizes and its copy on the right. The final translation example should show four permanently visible flag and wording options in a compact white panel.

Use the supplied reference as the final overall art direction while adapting it responsively rather than reproducing its desktop proportions literally on narrow phones.

Keep only meaningful product visuals: phone examples, translation preview, QR code, and Maps listing. The journey should converge into one updates message and finish with direct ways to contact HostingQr.

## Risks Or Tradeoffs

Side-by-side mobile nodes have limited width, so descriptions must stay concise and avoid technical language.
